place.name: Pantheon, Rome
place.description: The Pantheon (UK: , US: ; Latin: Pantheum, from Ancient Greek Πάνθειον (Pantheion) '[temple] of all the gods') is an ancient Polytheist temple in Rome, Italy, originally built under Roman emperor Augustus (27 BC–AD 14) and reconstructed under Hadrian (117–138). Since AD 609, it has served as the Roman Catholic Basilica of Saint Mary and the Holy Martyrs (Italian: Basilica di Santa Maria ad Martyres) with the special Pontifical privilege of immemorial status.
